title: Conserved quantities in a bosonic tight-binding chain with non-Hermitian quartic terms
abstract: We investigate local conserved quantities in non-Hermitian bosonic lattice systems whose underlying Yang--Baxter structure remains unclear. Focusing on a one-dimensional bosonic chain with quartic interactions of creation operators, we provide a new representation of the local conserved quantities previously constructed by Sanatani and Shiraishi. Using Fourier transformation and trigonometric identities, we systematically derive these conserved quantities and show directly that they form a mutually commuting family. We further extend the construction to interactions extending beyond a single site, cubic interactions, asymmetric hopping, and an on-site potential. Our results provide a unified framework for constructing and characterizing local conserved quantities in this class of non-Hermitian many-body systems.
summary: This work develops a general mathematical framework to find local conserved quantities in non-Hermitian bosonic chains with complex interactions. By using Fourier transforms and algebraic identities, the authors prove that these quantities commute, providing a powerful tool for analyzing the dynamics of such open quantum systems. This advances the understanding of integrability in non-Hermitian many-body physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and construction of local conserved quantities in non-Hermitian bosonic lattice systems, particularly when the underlying Yang-Baxter structure is unknown.
main_result: The authors provide a unified framework to systematically derive a family of mutually commuting local conserved quantities for bosonic chains with quartic interactions, extending the construction to include cubic terms and asymmetric hopping.
method: The primary methods involve using Fourier transformation and trigonometric identities to construct conserved charges, and employing advanced algebraic techniques like Newton-Girard formulas to prove necessary identities.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional bosonic tight-binding chain described by a Hamiltonian containing hopping terms (T) and various interaction terms (V), including quartic and cubic on-site interactions. The system is non-Hermitian.
key_observables: Local conserved quantities, $Q(n)$, which are shown to form a mutually commuting family, and the Hamiltonian $H$ itself, which is $Q(1)$.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the construction for the quartic model, proving mutual commutativity. It then systematically generalizes this framework to include cubic interactions, asymmetric hopping, and on-site potentials, detailing the mathematical machinery (like elementary symmetric polynomials) required for the construction.
why_interesting: The focus on non-Hermitian systems and finding exact conserved quantities is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics, dissipation, and the stability of quantum states in open quantum systems, linking directly to modern AMO and quantum transport theory.
